สร้าง UI สำหรับ setting Email agent โดยใช้ข้อมูลดังนี้

Description
As a ผู้ใช้งานระบบ (Admin / User)
I want มีหน้าจอ Agent Management เพื่อสร้างและตั้งค่า Agent ได้ด้วยตัวเอง
So that ฉันสามารถควบคุมการทำงานของ AI / Mail Agent ได้ตาม workflow ของบริษัท โดยไม่ต้องพึ่งทีมเทคนิค

-------------


1. Agent Management Overview
ระบบต้องมีเมนู Agent Management

ผู้ใช้งานสามารถ:



ดูรายการ Agent ทั้งหมดของ Company
เห็นสถานะ Agent (Active / Inactive)
สร้าง Agent ใหม่
แก้ไข / เปิด–ปิด Agent ที่มีอยู่
2. Create Agent
ผู้ใช้งานสามารถกด Create Agent ต้องสามารถตั้งค่า:



Agent Name (ไม่เกิน 120 characters)
Agent Type (เช่น Mail Agent)
ต้องสามารถบันทึกเป็น Draft หรือ Active ได้
3. Mail Agent Configuration
3.1 Email Scope
กำหนด Sender Email

และ/หรือ Receiver Email

เปิด / ปิดการใช้งาน filter ได้

3.2 Keyword Filter (ต่อยอดจากการ์ดก่อนหน้า)
กำหนด keyword จาก:

Email Subject

Email Body

เพิ่มได้มากกว่า 1 keyword

เปิด / ปิด keyword filter ได้

4. Drive & File Automation
ผู้ใช้งานสามารถตั้งค่า:

Auto Save File to Drive

Target Folder Path

ผู้ใช้งานสามารถตั้งค่า:

Auto Rename File

Auto Create Folder ตาม rule ที่กำหนด

เมื่อ Agent ทำงาน:

ไฟล์ต้องถูกจัดเก็บใน Drive

ใช้ชื่อไฟล์และโครงสร้าง folder ตาม configuration

5. Configuration Behavior
การเปลี่ยน configuration:

มีผลกับข้อมูลที่เข้ามา หลังจากตั้งค่า

ไม่กระทบข้อมูลที่ถูกประมวลผลไปแล้ว

ผู้ใช้งานสามารถเปิด / ปิด Agent ได้ทันที

6. Permission & Access
ผู้ใช้งาน (Admin / User ที่มีสิทธิ์) สามารถ:

สร้างและแก้ไข Agent ของ Company ได้

Agent และ configuration:

แยกตาม Company

ไม่สามารถเห็นหรือแก้ไขข้าม Company ได้

7. Audit & Log
ระบบต้องบันทึก log สำหรับ:

การสร้าง Agent

การแก้ไข configuration

การเปิด / ปิด Agent

Log ต้องระบุ:

ผู้กระทำ

วันที่และเวลา


Acceptance
     1. สิทธิ์การเข้าถึงตามบทบาท 
Admin เห็นเมนู/หน้าจอ Agent Management และทำได้ครบ: Create / Edit / Enable-Disable / Delete (หรือ Archive) / Publish (ถ้ามี)

User เห็นหน้าจอได้เฉพาะสิ่งที่ได้รับอนุญาต (เช่น View/Run/Assign) และ ไม่เห็นปุ่มที่ไม่มีสิทธิ์

หากผู้ใช้ไม่มีสิทธิ์เข้าถึง URL โดยตรง ระบบต้องปฏิเสธและแสดงข้อความ “ไม่มีสิทธิ์ใช้งาน”

2.หน้ารายการ Agents (List)

ระบบแสดงรายการ Agent พร้อมข้อมูล

Agent Name, Agent Type (AI / Mail), Status (Draft/Active/Inactive), Updated At, Updated By

มีค้นหา (Search) ตามชื่อ/ประเภท และมีตัวกรอง (Filter) ตาม Status/Type

คลิก 1 รายการต้องเข้า หน้ารายละเอียด/แก้ไข ได้

     3. สร้าง Agent ใหม่ได้ด้วยตัวเอง
Admin สามารถกด “สร้าง Agent” และบันทึกได้สำเร็จเมื่อกรอกข้อมูลที่จำเป็นครบ

ข้อมูลที่ต้องมีเพื่อบันทึก (อย่างน้อย):

Agent Name (บังคับ, ต้องไม่ซ้ำ)

Agent Type (บังคับ: AI Agent หรือ Mail Agent)

Description (ไม่บังคับ)

เมื่อบันทึกสำเร็จ ระบบต้องแสดง Agent ในรายการทันที

    4. ตั้งค่า Agent ให้รองรับ Workflow ของบริษัท
Agent ต้องสามารถถูก “ผูกกับ Workflow/Process” ของบริษัทได้อย่างน้อย 1 workflow

ในแต่ละ workflow ต้องกำหนดได้ว่า Agent ทำงานที่ “ขั้นตอน/Trigger” ใด (เช่น เมื่อสร้างเอกสาร/เมื่อเปลี่ยนสถานะ/ตามเวลา)

ระบบต้องไม่อนุญาตให้ Publish/Enable Agent หากยังไม่ได้กำหนด workflow/trigger ที่จำเป็น (ตาม rule ที่องค์กรตั้ง)

5.การตั้งค่าเฉพาะประเภท (AI Agent / Mail Agent)

หากเลือก AI Agent ต้องมีช่องตั้งค่าที่จำเป็น เช่น:

Input Source/Context (เลือกจากข้อมูลที่ระบบอนุญาต)

Output/Action ที่จะทำ (เช่น สร้างข้อความ/สรุป/จัดหมวดหมู่/แนะนำขั้นตอน)

หากเลือก Mail Agent ต้องมีช่องตั้งค่าที่จำเป็น เช่น:

From/Email Profile ที่ใช้ส่ง (เลือกจากที่ระบบตั้งไว้)

Recipient rule (เช่น ตามบทบาท/ตามข้อมูลในเอกสาร)

Subject/Body Template และตัวแปรที่รองรับ (Variables)

ระบบต้องแสดงฟิลด์ตาม Type ที่เลือก และซ่อนฟิลด์ที่ไม่เกี่ยวข้อง

6. ตรวจสอบความถูกต้องของข้อมูล (Validation)

Agent Name:

ห้ามว่าง, ต้องไม่ซ้ำ, ความยาวอยู่ในเกณฑ์ที่กำหนด

Start/End หรือ Schedule (ถ้ามี):

เวลาเริ่มต้องไม่มากกว่าเวลาสิ้นสุด

Template/Variables (ถ้ามี):

ตัวแปรที่ใช้ต้องอยู่ในรายการที่ระบบรองรับ มิฉะนั้นบันทึกไม่ได้และแจ้งชัดเจนว่าผิดตรงไหน

7.บันทึกแบบ Draft และการ Publish/Enable
เมื่อสร้างใหม่ ค่าเริ่มต้นเป็น Draft

Admin สามารถ:

Save Draft ได้ (ยังไม่ทำงานจริง)

Publish/Enable ได้เมื่อผ่าน validation ครบ

เมื่อ Enable แล้ว Agent ต้องถูกนับเป็น “Active” และพร้อมทำงานตาม trigger ที่ตั้งไว้


     8. ปิดการทำงาน (Disable) โดยไม่ลบข้อมูล
Admin สามารถ Disable Agent ได้

เมื่อ Disable แล้ว Agent ต้อง ไม่ถูกเรียกทำงาน ในทุก trigger/workflow ที่ผูกไว้ทันที (ตั้งแต่การประมวลผลครั้งถัดไป)


   
     9.ตั้งค่า Auto Save File to Drive



ในหน้าจอ Agent Management ต้องมีส่วนตั้งค่า Drive & File Automation

ผู้ใช้งาน (ตามสิทธิ์) สามารถเปิด/ปิดตัวเลือก Auto Save File to Drive

เมื่อเปิดใช้งาน ต้องสามารถระบุ Target Folder Path ได้

ระบบต้องตรวจสอบ Target Folder Path:

ต้องไม่ว่าง

ต้องเป็น path ที่ถูกต้องตามรูปแบบที่ระบบรองรับ

ต้องมีสิทธิ์เขียน (write) ใน path นั้น (อย่างน้อยในระดับ service account/agent account ที่ใช้บันทึก)


     10. ตั้งค่า Auto Rename File

ผู้ใช้งานสามารถเปิด/ปิดตัวเลือก Auto Rename File

หากเปิดใช้งาน ต้องสามารถกำหนดรูปแบบชื่อไฟล์ (Rename Rule) ได้ เช่น

Template/Pattern (รองรับตัวแปร เช่น{DocNo},{Date},{Customer},{AgentName}ตามที่ระบบกำหนด)

รองรับการกำหนดนามสกุลไฟล์ให้คงเดิมหรือเลือกตามประเภทไฟล์

ระบบต้อง validate รูปแบบชื่อไฟล์:

ห้ามมีอักขระต้องห้าม (เช่น/ \ : * ? " < > |หรืออื่น ๆ ตามข้อจำกัดของ Drive ที่ใช้)

ความยาวชื่อไฟล์ไม่เกินข้อจำกัดที่กำหนด

หากใช้ตัวแปรที่ไม่รองรับ ต้องบันทึกไม่ได้และแจ้งรายการตัวแปรที่อนุญาต


    11. ตั้งค่า Auto Create Folder ตาม Rule
ผู้ใช้งานสามารถเปิด/ปิด Auto Create Folder

หากเปิดใช้งาน ต้องกำหนด Folder Rule ได้อย่างน้อย:

โครงสร้างโฟลเดอร์แบบ Template เช่น/{Year}/{Month}/{DocType}/หรือ/{Customer}/{DocNo}/

ตัวแปรที่ใช้ต้องเป็นรายการที่ระบบรองรับ

ระบบต้อง validate Folder Rule:

ห้ามมีอักขระต้องห้าม

ต้อง resolve ตัวแปรแล้วได้ path ที่ถูกต้อง

กรณีโฟลเดอร์ปลายทางยังไม่มีอยู่ ระบบต้องสร้างโฟลเดอร์ตาม rule ให้โดยอัตโนมัต

 12 .ทดสอบการทำงาน (Test Run / Preview)

Admin สามารถกด “ทดสอบ” ได้ในหน้าจอ Agent (ก่อน Publish หรือหลัง Publish ก็ได้ตามที่กำหนด)

ระบบต้องแสดงผลลัพธ์การทดสอบ เช่น:

Input ที่ใช้ทดสอบ, Output ที่ได้, และ Log/ข้อความผิดพลาด (ถ้ามี)

การทดสอบต้อง ไม่กระทบข้อมูลจริง (เช่น ส่งเมลจริงต้องมีโหมดจำลอง/ส่งไป Sandbox/ผู้ทดสอบเท่านั้น

   
   13. Audit Log และการติดตามการเปลี่ยนแปลง
ทุกการ Create/Edit/Publish/Enable/Disable/Delete ต้องถูกบันทึก Audit อย่างน้อย:
ใครทำ, ทำเมื่อไหร่, ทำอะไร, ค่าเดิม/ค่าใหม่ (หรือสรุปการเปลี่ยนแปลง)  Dev ต้องสามารถตรวจสอบเหตุการณ์ย้อนหลังได้

   14. การจัดการข้อผิดพลาด (Error Handling)
หากบันทึกไม่สำเร็จ ระบบต้องแจ้งสาเหตุแบบ actionable (เช่น “ชื่อซ้ำ”, “ยังไม่ได้เลือก workflow”)
หาก Agent ทำงานล้มเหลวใน runtime ต้องมีสถานะ/Log ให้ตรวจสอบได้ และไม่ทำให้ระบบหลักล่ม

**Comprehending the Objective**

I'm now fully immersed in understanding the user's needs for a React application. My focus is on the core functionality: managing "Agents," specifically categorizing them into Email and AI agents. This mental framing will guide me as I work to develop a React application.


**Detailing Core Components**

I've broken down the features into core entities and agent types, focusing on the "Mail Agent" as the primary concern and now moving on to the "AI Agent". I'm structuring the features as dashboard/list views, create/edit forms, and their corresponding configurations. Key aspects include status tracking (Draft, Active, Inactive) and role-based permissions (Admin, User).


**Structuring the Architecture**

I'm now outlining a clear project structure. I'm finalizing the components: `AgentList`, `AgentForm`, `AuditLogViewer`, and a `TestRunModal`.  Type definitions for Agents, Logs, and Configurations are being carefully considered within `types.ts`. The design will be modern and user-friendly, with Tailwind.


**Implementing Data Persistence**

I'm now focusing on persistence via a mock service. I'm building out a `metadata.json` file for basic descriptions, and I'm developing detailed type definitions in `types.ts`, including `AgentType` and `AgentStatus` to ensure a robust typing structure. I am working on the initial layout, including a standard sidebar with Agent and Settings links, and a header. Key components like `AgentList` and `AgentForm` are next.


**Designing Tabular Forms**

I'm deep into the UI now, focusing on the form structure within the tabs. I'm building out a "General" tab and a tab for configuration, which will be dynamic based on Agent type. I'm also planning an "Automation" tab with toggles for common actions and helpful input field guidance, plus a "Test" tab, and a mock "Audit Log" display. I'm using `App.tsx` for managing the app-wide state and navigation, and I've opted for simple conditional rendering for view switching, to maintain the single-page application feel.


**Finalizing UI Features**

I'm now implementing the UI elements. I'm focusing on visual feedback, using status indicators; Green for Active, and Amber for Draft. Form controls will have `ring` focus states and standardized labels. I'm also adding simulated toast notifications for success and errors. Next, I am working on role-based permissions, variables, and audit log generation. I will also be working on testing functionality. I am now working on streamlining `AgentForm` to accommodate both agent types through conditional rendering. I will ensure that input fields are only visible when the respective toggles are activated.


**Consolidating Key Elements**

I've just finalized the basic directory structure, with index.html loading Tailwind and index.tsx mounting the App. I'm focusing on the type definitions now, creating types for Agent, Log, and Workflow in types.ts. The AgentList component will be a search/filter table, and I am building AgentForm to handle the complex form layout. App.tsx will be the state holder with routing logic and mock data initiation. I am making updates based on self-corrections while coding the form.

I'm checking the imports to ensure 'Filter' isn't being improperly used or misspelled within the context. The import statements are standard React ones so far.


**Correcting Missing Import**

I've identified the source of the `Filter` type error: a missing import. My focus has shifted to the `components/AgentForm.tsx` file, specifically examining the imports around line 354. I've pinpointed the issue and added the necessary `Filter` import from `lucide-react`, resolving the error.

I'm now going over the code in `components/AgentForm.tsx` to search for potential side effects. Although the `Filter` import fixed the initial error, I'm checking for other missing imports that might exist. I've spotted the usages of `PlusIcon`, `XIcon`, and `PowerIcon`, which are defined at the bottom. Also, I've checked the usages of other imports like `Mail`, `Bot`, `Save`, `FileCode`, `FolderOpen`, and `Beaker`, which are imported. I'm focusing on ensuring all used components and icons are properly imported.


**Assessing Icon Imports**

I'm making sure all the necessary icons are imported correctly, and I've verified the import of the `Play` icon on line 517. It appears that only the initial `Filter` import was missing. I'm now looking at constructing the XML representation, focusing on clearly documenting this import addition.

**Validating Input States**

I'm verifying the functionality of `handleInputChange` and `handleNestedChange`, particularly how they interact with `isReadOnly`, and updating the `formData` and `errors` states. Also, I'm checking the correct usage of the model options and input context source in the UI.

I'm checking the disabled state and making sure `handleNestedChange` is correctly updating the `formData.aiConfig.outputAction` state, ensuring the UI reflects the user's input. I've been drilling down on the specific logic needed for the preview function. I've defined the sample data I'll use to replace the variable placeholders in the rename pattern. I've also outlined the structure of the `generatePreview` function and where it should be located in `AgentForm.tsx`. My next step is to implement the function and integrate it into the UI.

I'm now integrating the `getPreviewFilename` function into `AgentForm.tsx`, specifically within the 'automation' tab where the `renamePattern` input resides. I need to ensure the preview updates dynamically as the user types, replacing placeholders like `{DocNo}` and `{Date}` with sample data. I also need to make sure the label "Preview:" is translatable, so I'll need to add a corresponding key to the `translations.ts` file.


**Considering Translation Implementation**

I'm now focusing on the translation aspect of the "Preview:" label. I've decided to add the `preview` key to `translations.ts` for consistency. I will add both English and Thai translations. Now that I know the contents of `translations.ts` from the last step, I'll proceed with updating the translation file before integrating the preview function into the `AgentForm`.


**Building the UI Elements**

I'm now integrating the preview display into the AgentForm, specifically next to the rename pattern input. I'm focusing on adding the preview div and styling it for better presentation, using a mono font and a slate background. Additionally, I've confirmed the `translations.ts` file needs the `labelPreview` key in both English and Thai. I'll construct the XML files, ensuring the translations are properly handled.


**Integrating Preview Logic**

I'm now integrating the final logic and the UI elements. I've defined `getRenamingPreview` inside the `AgentForm` component and I'm calling it within the render block for the 'automation' tab. I'm focusing on ensuring the preview updates correctly when the user modifies the renaming pattern, reflecting placeholder replacements like `{DocNo}` and `{Date}` with sample data. I'm also ensuring that the label, "Filename Preview", is pulled from the `translations.ts` file. I'll make sure the XML files are constructed properly.


**Refining XML Construction**

I'm now refining the construction of the XML files. Based on the previous steps, I'm working to include the preview display I constructed in `AgentForm.tsx`. I have the required translations and the preview logic set. I'm focusing on ensuring this is formatted correctly in the XML, and then will check that everything renders according to the design.

To implement the filename preview feature, I will:

1.  Update `translations.ts` to include a label for the preview.
2.  Update `components/AgentForm.tsx` to include a helper function that parses the rename pattern and replaces variables with sample data, then displays this preview below the input field.

payload.text: Change all ui to Antdesign components and all icons use Fontawesome (free version)

**Considering the Requirements**

I'm currently focused on dissecting the initial request. I've pinpointed the core goals: a UI library swap from a custom Tailwind setup to Ant Design, and an icon library shift from Lucide React to FontAwesome. My analysis is progressing; I'm mapping out the implications of each library change.


**Refining the Approach**

I'm now prioritizing the dependencies within the `index.html`. It's clear I need to inject Ant Design and FontAwesome CSS links, which, in this no-build environment, means direct injection. I'm also updating the `importmap` to accommodate Ant Design and its icons (considering `@ant-design/icons` or `react-fontawesome`). I'm leaning toward using classes directly from FontAwesome if the situation is simple, but `react-fontawesome` remains the React-compatible option.


**Analyzing Icon Strategy**

I've determined that the dependency complexity is high, given the single-file importmap. I am choosing a CDN-based FontAwesome approach (using `<i className="...">`) for simplicity and reliability. If easy, I may consider `react-fontawesome`, but not through esm.sh. I'm focusing now on updating `lucide-react` imports to the new FontAwesome equivalents. This should allow a straightforward transition for icons.


**Detailing Component Migrations**

I'm now deep into component-level replacements with Ant Design. I'm focusing on `Dropdown`, `Breadcrumb`, and `Button` swaps. Then, I'm tackling `AgentList.tsx`, replacing the HTML `table` with AntD's `Table`, custom pagination with its built-in feature, and various inputs with AntD components. I'm taking a senior engineer's view with `AgentForm.tsx`, emphasizing safe migration of the intricate state logic by replacing visual elements.


**Implementing UI Refinements**

I'm now integrating the remaining Ant Design replacements. I'm focusing on the conversion of the `Tabs` and `Alert` components. I am considering the `App.tsx`, which seems primarily for state, but I am verifying no direct UI rendering exists. I'll swap the `window.confirm` calls to utilize AntD's `Modal.confirm` for a better user experience. I am setting up the `ConfigProvider` for design token theming to align with the existing "Brand Blue". I'm getting ready to plan the implementation.


**Constructing Ant Design Components**

I'm now focusing on implementing the main layout components from Ant Design, specifically `Layout`, `Sider`, `Header`, and `Content`. I'm mapping the current navigation logic to use the Ant Design `Menu` items. After that, I will update `AgentList.tsx`, implementing the Ant Design `Table` with the appropriate `columns` definition and using the `Space` component for actions. payload.text: Change all icons to Lucid icon and change the CSS framework to Tailwind CSS

**Analyzing Iconography and Frameworks**

I'm currently focused on the shift from FontAwesome to Lucide icons within a Tailwind CSS framework. The existing implementation leverages Tailwind via CDN. I'm assessing the best approach for this migration, considering potential compatibility issues and optimization strategies. Next, I need to evaluate the required CSS class structure.


**Refining Icon Implementation**

I'm now thinking specifically about how to integrate `lucide-react` given the existing structure. It seems the best solution involves replacing the FontAwesome CDN and inline classes with `lucide-react` components. My main focus is now the `index.html` file, where I need to update the import map to include `lucide-react`. I believe this is the proper way, since I'm trying to replace the existing icons with React components. I will now integrate the new package by updating the `<script type="importmap">` tag.


**Adding Dependencies and Adjusting**

I've decided to add `"lucide-react": "https://esm.sh/lucide-react@0.294.0?deps=react@18.2.0"` to the import map. Next, I must systematically replace the FontAwesome icons throughout the project. I've compiled a list of files to check, specifically including `index.html`, `components/Layout.tsx`, `components/AgentList.tsx`, and `components/AgentForm.tsx`. I have also made an initial mapping of FontAwesome icons to their Lucide counterparts.


**Matching Icons to Lucide**

I've been creating a comprehensive mapping of FontAwesome icons to their Lucide equivalents. My focus has expanded to `AgentList.tsx` and `AgentForm.tsx`, pinpointing precise Lucide matches for icons such as `fa-robot`, `fa-envelope`, `fa-gears`, and other replacements. I'm now aiming to ensure visual consistency across the application.


**Considering Framework Migration Scope**

I'm now contemplating the impact of fully migrating from Ant Design to a Tailwind CSS-only framework. The current setup already incorporates Tailwind, mainly for utility classes and spacing, alongside extensive use of Ant Design components. Completely rewriting all UI components is a major undertaking that will require significant changes. I must weigh the effort against the benefits and assess the risks of breaking functionality. The current request is a broad one.


**Evaluating Framework Transition Scope**

I'm now determining the scope of moving from Ant Design to Tailwind. It seems like a complete rewrite of UI components, like `AgentForm.tsx`, is on the table, which imports all sorts of Ant Design components. Considering the potential work, it's clear this involves reimplementing things like the Layout, Table, Tabs, and various form controls. This is a very large undertaking, and it will require extensive changes to the existing structure. I am now reassessing the broad request from the user to see exactly what they're requesting.


**Clarifying Framework Objectives**

I'm now zeroing in on the user's intent: Are they aiming for visual improvements (icons), framework replacement (Tailwind), or both? The wording points strongly to a full Tailwind transition, which necessitates replacing Ant Design components. My immediate next step is to analyze the `index.html` file, removing AntD imports and adjusting styles, as well as checking the overall project structure to ensure this approach aligns with the user's ultimate goal. I need to be more precise about the user's intention here. I will remove the AntD imports and styles and replace them with Tailwind.


**Simplifying UI Components**

I'm now diving into the component replacements. I'll transform the `Layout`, `Header`, and `Content` sections into `div`s with Tailwind classes. The sidebar will have custom collapse logic, while dropdowns will be handled manually or simplified using details/summary elements. In `AgentList.tsx`, I'll replace the Ant Design Table with a standard HTML table styled with Tailwind, along with custom implementations for Buttons, Input, Select, and other components. `AgentForm.tsx` will similarly lose its Ant Design components, and I'll adapt form controls and layout with Tailwind's flex/grid system.


**Outlining Implementation Strategy**

I'm developing a structured plan for the UI overhaul. First, I'll update `index.html` to remove existing libraries and include Lucide-React. Then I will proceed in stages. `Layout.tsx` will be next. After that, I will rewrite `AgentList.tsx`, replacing the Ant Design table. Finally, I will adapt `AgentForm.tsx` to use Tailwind's form styles and layout tools, handling tabs with state management. I'm focusing on simplicity.


**Adapting Form and Lists**

The goal is to allow users to toggle between a sidebar navigation layout (the current setup) and a tab menu layout for the inner navigation. This flexibility aims to improve user experience in the Agent Management page.


**Implementing Horizontal Tabs**

I'm focusing on modifying the `AgentForm.tsx` file, introducing a state variable to manage the layout, and adding UI controls for switching. The next step involves refactoring the tab rendering logic within the component, so that it dynamically renders either the sidebar structure or the top tabs layout. My immediate concern is updating the component and making this logic seamless.

I've updated the component's state to control the `layoutMode`. I've added a switcher control to toggle between 'SIDEBAR' and 'TOP_TABS'. Currently, I'm refactoring the navigation section so that the correct structure, either sidebar or tabs, renders dynamically based on the state.

The sidebar tab needs full width and left border styling, while the horizontal tab design requires bottom border, padding, and other adjustments. **Analyzing UI Redesign** I'm currently focused on the redesign of the "Test Run" tab within the `AgentForm` component. The present interface is a bit basic; a console output. My goal is a more engaging and effective design, given the current context. I'm exploring different options to make the tab more user-friendly. **Reimagining Test Runs** My current focus is on transforming the "Test Run" tab into a more user-friendly, step-based UI, specifically for non-technical users. I'm moving away from the console-like output to a structured list of steps, visually indicating progress with checkmarks for completed stages like "Initialize Environment" and "Load Configuration." This enhancement is targeted at the `AgentForm` component in `components/AgentForm.tsx`, within the `activeTab === 'test'` section. I think this will greatly improve usability. **Structuring Test Execution** I'm currently fleshing out the step-by-step display for the "Test Run". I'm thinking of these steps: "Validate Configuration," "Check Permissions," "Input," "Apply Filters," and "Execute Actions." Each step needs a visual indicator: pending, running, completed (checkmark), or failed (red X). The "Run Test" button will initiate the sequence. I'm focusing on granular state management—likely an array of step statuses—to drive the UI animation. I will convert the existing mock success result. **Visualizing Test Flow** I'm now fully immersed in the "Test Run" UI. The planned steps are: "Setup Environment," "Simulate Trigger," "Process Rules," and "Generate Output." I'm updating the `runTest` function to reset these to 'PENDING', then iterate, simulating progress with running then complete states, using a delay. The layout of the test tab is taking shape too. It starts with "Ready to test" and a "Start" button, transitioning to a vertical step list with icons. Finally, a success card summarizes results. I am modifying the `AgentForm.tsx` file for the test steps and state. **Implementing Step-wise Test** I've been working on refining the `runTest` logic and am using `setTimeout` chains with delays to update each step's status sequentially. I'm also starting to render the step list and making sure to update the visual styles to match the new UI's friendly design, moving away from the black console style. I'm focused on clean text, a white background, and distinct icons. In `translations.ts`, I'm adding new translations for the steps if needed, or reusing existing ones, focusing on being bilingual. **Simplifying Test State** I'm now streamlining the state management for the test run. I've switched from detailed step-by-step statuses to a simpler `testProgress` counter and `testStatus` string. The `TEST_STEPS` constant is defined, containing each step's label and description, and I'll adapt the `runTest` function for it. I am also planning on adding the new keys to `translations.ts` file for localization. I think this will improve code readability. **Refining Test Workflow** I've just added the `runTest` function to update the `testProgress` in a loop, simulating the progress. I've switched over to the new UI structure, which has a conditional display depending on the `testStatus`: showing an idle screen with a "Start Test" button, or the step-by-step progress when the test is running. The component layout now includes a loading icon and step updates, and I will be working on the translation file. ```jsx )} ``` **Defining Step Visuals** I'm now focusing on refining the visual representation of each test step within the "Test Run" UI. I'm aiming for a clear timeline-like layout for non-technical users. The icons for each step now need to be defined. I've been adding the needed keys into `translations.ts` file. **Implementing Test Display** I'm now fully immersed in updating the `AgentForm.tsx` file for the new test display. I'm importing the `Loader2` icon and replacing the old console output with my new UI. I'm working to get all icons displayed properly, including the checkmark for completion. I am currently focusing on getting the `TEST_STEPS` constant and the test progress re-renders to display the proper data. **Visualizing Final Steps** I'm working on the design for the final result card, and I'll reuse the structure from the mock successful test to display the test results. I will be incorporating descriptions in both Thai and English. I've defined the steps: Environment, Config, Connections, Simulation, and Completion. My current focus is implementing the translations in `translations.ts` and updating the `AgentForm.tsx` file for a final result display. I will ensure that the character limit constraints are still applied to the form. **Defining Test Visuals** I'm now diving into the specifics of the new test interface. The initial focus is making the test tab user-friendly and intuitive, specifically for non-technical users. I am creating a vertical list to show the test steps, with each step getting a unique icon for visual representation. I am adding icons for each step in the `translations.ts` file, and I am importing the `Loader2` icon and replacing the old console output with my new UI in the `AgentForm.tsx` file.

To implement the requested Step-based UI for the Test Run tab, I will update `translations.ts` to include the step descriptions and `components/AgentForm.tsx` to replace the console-like interface with a user-friendly progress stepper.

payload.text:
test run
ขอเป็นแบบ UI แบบ step ให้ user non tech เข้าใจง่ายๆ ขั้นไหนผ่านแล้วเป็น check ถูก

ขอคำแบบเข้าใจง่ายๆ ทั้ง en/th user non-tech ใช้งาน อ่านแล้วเข้าใจได้เลย ว่าระบบกำลังทำอะไรบ้าง

**Developing a UI Flow**

I'm currently focused on the `AgentForm` component's "Test Run" UI. The goal is to visually represent the test run process as a simple, step-by-step flow, making it intuitive for non-technical users. Each completed step will be marked with a checkmark to create a sense of progress.


**Implementing Test Run Details**

I've just added simplified text for each test step, creating a better understanding of the process. I'm focusing on user-friendly phrasing in both English and Thai. Next, I will be working on the UI implementation.


**Refining Test Step Language**

I've just been refining the test step labels and descriptions for the UI. I replaced some terminology with simpler, more accessible language. For instance, the steps are now described as "Preparing System," "Checking Rules," and "Connecting Services." The Thai versions are also being translated and simplified for better user understanding.


**Revising Test Step Verbiage**

I'm now revising the test step wording to align with the visual style the user prefers. I've noted "ตัวจำลองการทดสอบ" and "ประมวลผลข้อมูลจำลองตามกฎ" are key phrases from the screenshot requirements. My focus is to create concise descriptions for each test step, such as "เตรียมระบบ", "ตรวจสอบกฎ", "เชื่อมต่อบริการ", "เริ่มจำลองงาน", and "สรุปผล."


**Designing a Test UI**

I'm now designing the test UI based on the user's specific feedback, focusing on simplicity for non-technical users. The "ทดสอบใหม่" (Restart Test) button is in place. I'm working on a vertical layout with icons for each step, and a result box at the bottom. I'm also simplifying the steps as requested.


**Updating Test Descriptions**

I've just updated the test step descriptions with simpler language, both in English and Thai. I've rephrased "Preparing System" and "Checking Rules" to be more accessible. The goal is clarity for all users, including those less familiar with the technical details.


**Adding Data Processing Steps**

I'm now integrating the new test steps. I've added "ลองประมวลผลข้อมูลตามเงื่อนไข" for data processing and "สรุปผลลัพธ์การทดสอบทั้งหมด" for saving the results. The UI is being refactored to use vertical steps with specific visual cues for completed, current, and pending steps. The test status determines the styling, and the "Start Test" button triggers the process.


**Crafting Step Logic**

I'm now implementing the UI logic to represent test step states: current, pending, and completed, based on the `testProgress` value. I'm also ensuring the `AgentForm` updates `testProgress` with delays. The focus is on preparing the XML and `AgentForm` for the "Test Steps" section update, reusing the existing `TEST_STEPS` array but relying on the updated translation keys. Finally, I'm refining the step descriptions for easy understanding by non-technical users.


**Structuring the UI Flow**

I'm now structuring the UI based on the vertical list layout from the screenshot requirements. I am using icons, titles, and descriptions, to represent each test step. The `runTest` function will be updated to manage the flow, including test status, resetting test results, and managing the `testProgress` within the loop. The new test steps are to be "เตรียมพื้นที่ทดสอบ...", "ตรวจสอบเงื่อนไข", "ทดสอบเข้าถึงอีเมลและไดรฟ์...", "ประมวลผลตามกฎที่ตั้งไว้...", and "รวบรวมผลลัพธ์...". I am focusing on making the steps clear and easy to follow.


**Implementing Test State Logic**

I'm now implementing the UI logic to clearly represent the different states of each test step, based on the `testProgress` and `testStatus` values. When `testProgress` indicates the current step, it shows as running; steps before are completed, with a green checkmark; and steps after are pending, grayed out. I'm taking care of the edge case for `COMPLETED` status, and ensuring all steps are marked as completed.


**Refining Step State Logic**

I've just refined the logic for step states, simplifying it significantly. Now, if the `testStatus` is "COMPLETED," all steps are marked as such. If it's "IDLE," they're all pending. During "RUNNING," a step is completed if its ID is less than the current `testProgress`, it's running if IDs equal, and it's pending if its ID is greater than the current `testProgress`. The logic now directly corresponds to how the tests are run sequentially.


**Visualizing Test Progress**

I'm now focusing on implementing the visual components for each test step, drawing inspiration from existing icons. I'm leveraging `CheckCircle`, `Loader2`, and `Circle` icons to represent completed, running, and pending states, respectively. The UI logic now dictates the colors and icons, and a connecting vertical line visually links the steps. Additionally, I'll style the result box to create a nicer visual experience, and I am updating the `AgentForm` to reflect the improvements.

To update the "Test Run" UI to be more user-friendly for non-technical users with a step-by-step visual indicator and simplified text, I will modify `translations.ts` and `components/AgentForm.tsx`.

### **Specification**

1.  **Translations (`translations.ts`)**:
    *   Simplify "Test Steps" descriptions to be very clear and jargon-free (e.g., "Checking Rules" instead of "Validate Configuration").
    *   Ensure both English and Thai translations convey the action clearly.

2.  **Agent Form (`components/AgentForm.tsx`)**:
    *   **Test Tab Layout**:
        *   Move the "Test Simulator" header and "Start Test" button inside a main card container.
        *   Replace the console log style with a vertical stepper list.
        *   Each step item will have an icon (Check for done, Spinner for working, Circle for waiting) and a description.
        *   Connect steps with a vertical line to visualize the flow.
    *   **Logic**:
        *   When `testStatus` is `COMPLETED`, all steps show as checked.
        *   When `testStatus` is `RUNNING`, steps before the current one are checked, current is spinning, others are gray.
    *   **Result Box**:
        *   Style the final result box with a friendly green background (`bg-emerald-50`) to indicate success clearly.

### **Code Changes**

สร้างหน้า tracking รายการเป็นหน้า default เอาไว้สำหรับรับรายการมีทั้ง upload, mail agent, api
- นำเมนูตั้งค่า agent management ไปไว้มี่เมนู profile มุมขวาบน ที่มีรูป avatar แบบ text เมื่อกดแล้วแสดงเมนูย่อย (agent management, user management, logout) เมื่อกด เมนู agent management ถึงเจอหน้า tracking agent management

**Considering The Task**

I'm currently focused on the initial request analysis. My primary goal is to determine the best approach for a default "Tracking" page. I need to integrate various data sources: uploads, a mail agent, and an API. I'm also considering how the proposed navigation changes will impact the overall flow.


**Prioritizing Navigation Updates**

I've just refined the navigation changes. "Agent Management" will be moved to the user profile dropdown, alongside "User Management" and "Logout." This impacts the layout and where users find critical features. I'm focusing on user experience, and this change streamlines the sidebar. I'm now exploring data types needed for tracking.


**Developing The Interface**

I'm now deep in the design phase. I've defined the table structure, including checkbox, and `TrackingItem` columns. Row actions will include View, History/Log, Send, and Delete. I plan standard pagination. I'm focusing on UI elements, and now plan to address layout and routing.


**Outlining The Implementation**

I'm now detailing the implementation steps. I've focused on `translations.ts` and adding the required strings. Next, I plan to build `TrackingPage.tsx` with its header, filter grid, table, and pagination. Layout changes are next, with sidebar and profile dropdown modifications. Finally, I'll update the application state in `App.tsx` for view management.


**Connecting the Navigation**

I'm now integrating the `onNavigate` function into `Layout` to enable the profile dropdown to control view changes. I'm focusing on UI adjustments and expanding the implementation. I've begun modifying the `translations.ts` file to accommodate the translated text. The focus is now on syncing the navigation triggers.


**Finalizing the Integration**

I'm currently finalizing the navigation, focusing on hooking up routing. I've added the `onNavigate` prop and integrated `TrackingPage` into `App.tsx`, adding the logic for `currentView`. I'm updating `translations.ts` and `Layout.tsx`, concentrating on the sidebar icon and profile dropdown menu updates. Finally, I'm integrating the types for tracking, and I'm adding "Agent Management" to the profile dropdown.


**Confirming the Handlers**

I'm now implementing the navigation handlers. I'm focusing on ensuring `App.tsx` passes the navigation handler to `Layout`. The goal is to facilitate seamless view changes. My focus is on the crucial connection between the application and the layout for correct routing of interactions. I'll need to double check the layout requirements as well.


**Adjusting The Views**

I'm now revising the app's structure. I've removed "Agent Management" from the sidebar, and made "Document Tracking" the new default. I've also added "Agent Management" to the profile dropdown for easier access. The `currentView` in `App.tsx` will default to 'TRACKING', and I'll handle all view switches. I'm focusing on the XML now.

Here is the implementation plan to satisfy your request:

1.  **Create `components/TrackingPage.tsx`**: A new component that implements the UI shown in the screenshot (Filters, Table with specific columns/badges, and Pagination).
2.  **Update `types.ts`**: Add necessary data types for the tracking items.
3.  **Update `translations.ts`**: Add English and Thai translations for the new Tracking page.
4.  **Update `components/Layout.tsx`**: 
    *   Remove "Agent Management" from the sidebar.
    *   Add "Document Tracking" to the sidebar.
    *   Update the Profile Dropdown to include the "Agent Management" link.
    *   Add a navigation handler prop.
5.  **Update `App.tsx`**: 
    *   Set the default view to the new Tracking Page.
    *   Manage navigation state between Tracking and Agent Management.

เมนู อัปโหลดไฟล์เอกสาร
- รองรับไฟล์  PDF, JPG, JPEG, PNG เท่านั้น ไฟล์ละไม่เกิน 5MB และอัปโหลดพร้อมกันได้สูงสุด 10 ไฟล์เท่านั้น
- เมื่ออัปโหลดเสร็จจะพาไปหน้า tracking รายการ แล้วไปสร้างรายการตามไฟล์ที่อัปโหลดมา

**Defining Upload Behavior**

Okay, I'm focusing on the "Upload Document" functionality based on the mockups. My initial direction is to create a drag-and-drop area for uploads, with file type validation for PDFs, JPGs, JPEGs, and PNGs. I need to figure out the maximum file size.


**Refining Upload Interface**

I've set the file size limit to 5MB each, with a maximum of 10 files per upload. The interface will feature a list displaying file details including file name, type, and size. There will be "Clear All" and "Upload All" buttons. A modal will display validation errors. I've also outlined the logic flow, including a redirect to the "Document Tracking" page after a successful upload. Finally, I’ve considered empty and populated states based on the visual designs, which will inform the final layout of the UI elements.


**Detailing Error Handling**

I'm now detailing the "Upload Document" functionality based on the latest mockups and feedback. I'm focusing on the specifics for the interface. I've designed the UI with "Delete All" and "Upload All" buttons, an error modal with a clear title and a list of reasons for upload failures. I'm refining the user experience.

**Component Architecture**

I'm starting to formalize the implementation. I plan to create a new `UploadPage.tsx` component to handle file uploads. I'm considering using either the HTML5 drag and drop API or a simple input. The file upload and error modal are handled locally within this component. I'm also planning to refactor App.tsx to manage the `trackingData` state and handle navigation to the new upload view, which should update the `trackingData` and switch the view to `TRACKING` after upload. The `TrackingPage.tsx` will be modified to accept the updated data.


**Implementing Navigation Logic**

I'm now focusing on integrating the upload functionality with the application's navigation. I'll modify the `Layout.tsx` component to make sure the sidebar's "Upload Document" button routes correctly to the new `UPLOAD` view. I'm also adding the necessary translation keys for the upload page, specifically for drag text, column headers, buttons, and error messages.


**Orchestrating the Code**

I'm making progress. I'm focusing on the implementation by starting with new translations for the "Upload Document" labels and content. I'm moving to the `UploadPage.tsx` component, developing the drag-and-drop logic using `useDropzone` logic. I'm now also adding the table rendering and validation logic, with the error modal. Finally, I'm working on the data state in `App.tsx` and moving the mock data. I am passing the data down to `TrackingPage`, passing the `onUpload` callback to `UploadPage`. The goal is to get this data in a mock structure.


**Refining Translations**

I've added the specific translation keys I need for the Upload page. I have incorporated the updated copy for the drag-and-drop text, the column headers, and button labels. I have also added error messages for file uploads. The error keys are ready, including the descriptive text and requirements.

To implement the "Upload Document" feature, I will create a new `UploadPage` component, update the main `App` to manage tracking data state (so new uploads appear in the list), and update the navigation logic.

Here are the changes:

1.  **`translations.ts`**: Added translations for the upload screen (drag & drop text, table headers, error messages).
2.  **`components/UploadPage.tsx`**: Created the new upload interface with drag-and-drop, file validation (PDF, JPG, PNG, Max 5MB, Max 10 files), file listing, and error handling modal.
3.  **`components/TrackingPage.tsx`**: Updated to accept `items` as a prop instead of using static internal data, allowing it to display newly uploaded files.
4.  **`components/Layout.tsx`**: Updated navigation handling to support the new 'UPLOAD' view.
5.  **`App.tsx`**:
    *   Lifted tracking data state to `App` component.
    *   Added the `UPLOAD` view case.
    *   Implemented `handleUpload` to convert uploaded files into tracking items and redirect to the tracking list.

I'm now focusing on how the user will interact with Excel data within the application. The goal is to provide a UI that enables structured data extraction from an Excel file. I'm imagining a spreadsheet viewer, simulating a grid layout, on the left pane. The right pane will maintain its data mapping functionality to translate the raw file contents into business data. **Simplifying the Extraction Logic**

I'm now simplifying the extraction logic, deciding to initially focus on single-record scenarios. I'm assuming each Excel file represents a single transaction or a specific row from a larger list. สำหรับการจัดการไฟล์ Excel ที่มาจาก Email Agent ระบบควรมีการแสดงผลที่แตกต่างจาก PDF เนื่องจากธรรมชาติของข้อมูลที่เป็นตาราง (Structured Data) แทนที่จะเป็นรูปภาพเอกสาร (Unstructured Document)

นี่คือแนวคิดและ UI ที่ผมออกแบบให้:

1.  **UI ฝั่งซ้าย (Source Viewer)**: เปลี่ยนจาก PDF Viewer เป็น **"Spreadsheet Viewer"**
    *   แสดงข้อมูลในรูปแบบตาราง (Grid) เหมือนโปรแกรม Excel
    *   มี Tab ด้านล่างเพื่อเลือก Sheet
    *   **Highlight Row/Cell**: เมื่อข้อมูลถูก Extract มาจากแถวไหน ระบบจะ Highlight แถวนั้นให้เด่นชัด เพื่อให้ User รู้ว่าข้อมูลชุดนี้มาจากบรรทัดไหนของไฟล์

2.  **UI ฝั่งขวา (Data Form)**:
    *   ยังคงแสดงแบบฟอร์ม Invoice (เลขที่, วันที่, ยอดเงิน) เหมือนเดิม
    *   **เพิ่มฟีเจอร์ "Column Mapping"**: แสดงให้เห็นว่าข้อมูลช่องนี้ ดึงมาจาก Column ไหนของ Excel (เช่น "Invoice No" มาจาก "Column A")

3.  **การจัดการข้อมูล (Data Management)**:
    *   เนื่องจาก 1 ไฟล์ Excel อาจมีหลายรายการ (Multiple Invoices in one file)
    *   ในหน้า Tracking โดยปกติ 1 Row คือ 1 Transaction หากไฟล์ Excel นั้นถูกแตกเป็นหลาย Transaction แล้ว หน้า Extraction นี้จะโฟกัสที่ **Row ที่เกี่ยวข้องกับ Transaction นั้น**
    *   แต่ถ้า 1 ไฟล์ = 1 รายการ ระบบจะอ่านข้อมูลสรุปจากเซลล์ต่างๆ มาแสดง

ผมจะทำการอัปเดตไฟล์ดังนี้:
1.  `App.tsx`: เพิ่ม Mock Data ที่เป็นไฟล์ `.xlsx` จาก Email Agent
2.  `components/ExtractionView.tsx`: เพิ่ม Logic การแสดงผลแบบ Excel Viewer

1.  **Interactive Column Mapping (Click-to-Map):** Instead of searching through long dropdowns, users can click a "Target" button on a field, then simply click the desired column header in the Excel grid to link them.
2.  **Visual Feedback:**
    *   **Highlighting:** When a user focuses on a field, the corresponding column in the Excel grid will highlight.
    *   **Badges:** Mapped columns will show a badge indicating which field they are linked to.
3.  **Large Dataset Handling:**
    *   Expanded the Mock Data to simulate a real-world scenario with many columns.
    *   The Grid View is optimized for horizontal scrolling while keeping the "Form" fixed.

I'm leaning toward a slide-out effect using conditional rendering or a width transition for a cleaner look.


**Implementing Panel Dynamics**

This involves replacing the current button text with the translated versions for improved usability. I'm focusing on the "Map Column" button, and will replace the hardcoded text with the new translation keys. I will work with both English and Thai.

payload.text:
อ่านไฟล์ excel
- เมื่อมีการเลือก column เพื่อเปลี่ยนการ mapping หัวข้อใน  card ด้านขวาต้องเปลี่ยนตาม column ที่เลือกด้วย
- แปลไทยส่วนที่เกี่ยวกับกรอบสีส้มตามรูปอ้างอิง

**Refining Excel Handling**

payload.text:
อ่านไฟล์ excel
- สามารถเพิ่ม card ด้านขวามือได้จาก ชุดตัวแปรที่มีกำหนดไว้ให้ตามแล้วแต่ชุดข้อมูลที่เลือกมาให้สามารถเลือกเพิ่ม card เพื่อทำ mapping กับ data ของ excel เพิ่มได้
- ไม่สามารถเพิ่มตัวแปรแบบอิสระ ที่ไม่ได้กำหนดไว้ในชุดข้อมูลได้
- สลับลำดับ card ของชุดตัวแปรได้

**Analyzing Extraction Form**

I'm currently focused on improving how the Excel file mapping is managed within the `ExtractionView` component. Specifically, I'm analyzing the "Extraction Form" (right-side panel) and the current Excel file mapping implementation. My goal is to determine ways to enhance the user experience and streamline the mapping process in this area.


**Refining Field Management**

I'm now implementing the ability to add and reorder fields in the extraction form. I'm focusing on defining a set of predefined variables related to the "dataset" and managing two lists: one for currently displayed fields (`activeFields`) and another for available, non-displayed fields (`availableFields`). I'm removing the old "custom metadata" functionality to align with the dataset-based variable restriction.


**Implementing Field Controls**

I've removed the custom metadata functionality and implemented an "Add Field" mechanism, presenting available fields in a dropdown for selection to add them to the active list. Additionally, I'm working on enabling the reordering of the fields within the active fields list, opting for simple "Move Up" and "Move Down" buttons on each card for a robust and user-friendly interface. Finally, a delete button is added for easy field removal.


**Defining Field Availability**

I'm now focusing on the UI for adding and managing fields within the extraction form. I'm prioritizing an intuitive "Add Field" interaction and incorporating clear controls for reordering and removing fields. I'm also expanding the predefined field list to include a set of "E-Declaration" fields, enhancing the system's flexibility. My current focus is on the interaction flow, enabling users to add, map, and reorder fields efficiently. I also plan to refactor the code to remove the `TagInput` component and the `metadataTags` state, updating the `fields` state and introducing a `ALL_AVAILABLE_FIELDS` constant.


**Implementing Field Controls**

I've been working on new functions: `handleAddField(fieldId)`, `handleRemoveField(fieldId)`, and `handleMoveField(index, direction)`. I've updated the UI to render a loop of `activeFields`, complete with controls for moving up, down, and removing. I also added the "Add Field" button/dropdown at the bottom. I'm focusing on the "Dataset: E-Declaration" concept, creating a static list but structuring the code to give the impression of a dynamic data source. I am focusing on this because drag and drop implementation would be error-prone without external libraries.


**Enhancing Field Controls**

I'm now implementing new field controls within the UI. I'm choosing between visible "Move Up" and "Move Down" buttons or incorporating them into a "More Options" menu for better space management. Additionally, I'm integrating an "Add Field" button that will activate a native select or custom dropdown, enhancing the user's field selection experience. I'm focusing on the updates to `ExtractionView.tsx` and incorporating `DATASET_FIELDS`.


**Implementing Field Availability**

I've been working on integrating a controlled dropdown for adding fields from a predefined list (`DATASET_FIELDS`). I'm using `availableFields`, derived dynamically from the current `fields` state, to ensure only available fields are selectable. The dropdown triggers an `addField` function that updates the `fields` state with the selected field, and the `removeField` function now filters the correct field out of the `fields` state. I'm focusing on making the logic efficient. I'm also planning to update translations if needed.


**Adding Translation Requirements**

I'm now focusing on ensuring that any new UI text introduced, such as "Add Field," "Remove," and "Move Up/Down," has appropriate translations, especially in Thai. I will add these translations to `translations.ts` for consistency. I also confirmed that removing the custom tag input is correct, aligning with the "dataset" restriction. I will refine the `fields` state initialization, ensuring it matches `DATASET_FIELDS`. I will update `DATASET_FIELDS` to match the initial fields.


**Refining Reordering Mechanics**

I'm now focusing on reordering. I've opted for a click-based "Move Up" and "Move Down" button approach for reordering fields, which is simpler and more reliable than HTML5 drag-and-drop for this context. These buttons, alongside the existing "Remove" button, will provide a straightforward and user-friendly interface for field manipulation, aligning with the "สลับลำดับ card ของชุดตัวแปรได้" requirement.


**Updating Translation Requirements**

I'm now prioritizing the `translations.ts` updates. I've prepared all the necessary translations for new UI elements, including "Add Field," "Remove," "Move Up/Down," and related prompts in both English and Thai. I'll integrate these translations into the component. I'm also confirming the removal of the TagInput and metadataTags states. Additionally, I'll introduce a FieldCard component or inline to handle the UI.


**Implementing Field Display**

I'm now focusing on rendering each field card within the UI, including the new controls. My next steps involve incorporating the "Move Up," "Move Down," and "Remove" buttons into each field card, making the field management process intuitive. I'm also ensuring that my `DATASET_FIELDS` covers potential mappings for the `EXCEL_DATA` headers, like 'Ref ID', 'Inv Date', etc. I'm working on the dropdown for the pre-defined fields to be added.


**Refining Field Rendering**

I'm now focusing on integrating the updated field controls, specifically the "Move Up," "Move Down," and "Remove" icons within each field card. I am planning to represent the standard icon, plus the "trash" icon for removal, and the arrow up and down icons for reordering. I'm working to consolidate `fields` state for `id`, `label`, `value`, and `mappedColIndex`. I'm also planning to create a `masterFields` constant to represent a list of definitions.


**Updating Field Mapping**

I'm now making final adjustments to the field mapping logic. I'm focusing on ensuring initial state uses labels matching the dataset definitions to prevent duplicate entries in the "Add" dropdown. I'm updating the `fields` state initialization to be a subset of the `DATASET_DEFS`. I'm integrating the provided IDs, and I'm updating the `fields` state to match the labels.


**Implementing Field Logic**

I'm now implementing the core field management functions. I've defined `moveField`, `removeField`, and `addField`, ensuring that the UI updates the fields state correctly. I'll include the translations for `btnAddField` and `lblAvailableFields`. My current focus is integrating these methods to make the UI interactive.


**Clarifying Label Interaction**

I'm now clarifying the requirement: Does "เปลี่ยนหัวข้อใน card" mean changing the **label** of the field card dynamically based on the selected Excel column? It appears the user expects the field label (e.g., "Invoice Date") to change to the selected column's name (e.g., "Customer Name") if mapped. I'm considering the potential implications and whether this aligns with standard extraction tool conventions. It sounds like renaming the field.


**Clarifying Column Mapping**

I'm now clarifying the intended functionality related to column mapping within the field cards. I'm focusing on the "เปลี่ยนหัวข้อใน card" requirement, specifically, the interaction between selecting an Excel column and updating the field card. The user appears to be indicating the card's label should change to match the selected Excel column when a mapping is established, and the provided images further solidify this assumption. I'm focusing on the expected behavior of mapping a field to a column.


**Interpreting Mapping Updates**

I'm now carefully interpreting the requirement regarding field label updates during column mapping. The key is to clarify whether the field card *label* (e.g., "Invoice Date") itself should change to the selected Excel column name (e.g., "Inv Date"). It seems the user intends the "Source Label" inside the card, representing the source column, to update based on the mapping. I've re-read and analyzed the provided context.


**Interpreting Column Mapping**

I'm now focusing on the precise interpretation of column mapping updates based on recent user interactions. Given the new screenshot and "change the header" phrasing, I believe the intention is for the "Source: Col B (Inv Date)" label within the field card to reflect the selected Excel column upon mapping, *not* the card's main label or value. I'm focusing on the integration of this update with the current mapping implementation.


**Implementing Card Management**

I'm now focusing on implementing the main "Add/Remove/Reorder" card management features. This requires updating the `DATASET_DEFS` definitions and the associated translations. I will include the translations for these new UI elements. The intention is for card management to represent mapping logic.

The `ExtractionView` component has been updated to implement the requested features:

1.  **Predefined Field Management**:
    *   Removed the "Custom Metadata" (free-text tag input) section.
    *   Added a "Dataset: E-Declaration" logic with a predefined set of available variables (Invoice Number, Tax ID, Branch, etc.).
    *   Added an **"Add Field"** button at the bottom of the list, allowing users to select and add only fields defined in the dataset.

2.  **Card Reordering & Removal**:
    *   Each card now has a **Menu** (⋮) with options to:
        *   **Move Up / Move Down**: Reorder the cards within the list.
        *   **Remove**: Remove the card from the active list (returning it to the available pool).

3.  **Dynamic Source Mapping**:
    *   Preserved the logic where mapping a column updates the card to show the Column Header (e.g., "Source: Col B (Inv Date)"), fulfilling the requirement for the card information to reflect the selected column.
